doc.title: Billy Bauer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: Making your own record date, then versus now
summary: Rowe asks if he would have made his own record at 21; Bauer says no, recalling a time with only an old victrola.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: I hope you have a lot of cuts.

Oh we can cut and snip if we want. But you said an interesting thing about how some of the younger players come to you and they make their own record dates and the whole thing. Would it have occurred to you, when you were let’s say 21, to go out and make your own record?

No. I didn’t think of that at all. But that’s the way the world is today. But then again I’m saying in the beginning, a record date, was like I didn’t even have a place and I had an old victrola. You know so records was like — I could go back so far, that radio wasn’t even – that’s a long time.
